name: Cycles
description: John Doe started thinking about graphs. After some thought he decided that he wants to paint an undirected graph, containing exactly k cycles of length 3 . A cycle of length 3 is an unordered group of three distinct graph vertices a , b and c , such that each pair of them is connected by a graph edge. John has been painting for long, but he has not been a success. Help him find such graph. Note that the number of vertices there shouldn't exceed 100 , or else John will have problems painting it.
input_specification: A single line contains an integer k ( 1 ≤ k ≤ 10 5 ) — the number of cycles of length 3 in the required graph.
output_specification: In the first line print integer n ( 3 ≤ n ≤ 100 ) — the number of vertices in the found graph. In each of next n lines print n characters " 0 " and " 1 ": the i -th character of the j -th line should equal " 0 ", if vertices i and j do not have an edge between them, otherwise it should equal " 1 ". Note that as the required graph is undirected, the i -th character of the j -th line must equal the j -th character of the i -th line. The graph shouldn't contain self-loops, so the i -th character of the i -th line must equal " 0 " for all i .
approach_summary: Verify predicate monotonicity: P(x) is true for x ≤ K and false otherwise. Binary search over the answer domain to find the boundary in O(log(Range) × Verify_Time).

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 232A — Cycles [33. Binary Search]
topic_editorial.summary: Binary search on the monotonic answer domain.
topic_editorial.key_invariant: The predicate function $P(x)$ ('Is answer $\le x$ feasible?') is monotonic: if $P(x)$ is true for some value, it remains true for all larger values (or vice versa). This allows binary division of the answer search space $[\text{low}, \text{high}]$ in $O(\log(\text{Range}))$.
topic_editorial.complexity_analysis:
- **Time Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(N \log(\text{Range}))$
  The binary search divides the search interval by 2 at each iteration, requiring $\log_2(\text{Range})$ steps. In each step, the feasibility check `check(mid)` scans the array in $\mathcal{O}(N)$ time.
- **Space Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(1)$ auxiliary space
  The algorithm operates directly over the input array without allocating extra auxiliary memory.
